title: A trim request the API can trust

blocks.text: A vegetation team plans which overhead circuits to trim this season. Their scheduling tool will call an API with a JSON body like this:

The optimizer behind the API trusts its input: a negative budget or a repeated circuit would build a model that answers a question nobody asked. So the API must refuse such a request with a 422 before any model is built, and say which field is wrong.
In `trim_api.py`, add the rules to the two pydantic models. The endpoint is written. The rules:

items: `budget` is a whole number of $k, zero or more. A zero budget is a real request: trim nothing.
`circuits` has at least one circuit, and no two circuits share a `circuit_id`.
A circuit's `circuit_id` is not empty, its `miles` is above zero, and its `cost` is zero or more.
A field the API does not know, at the top or inside a circuit, is refused, not ignored: a misspelled `budjet` must never fall back to a default.

blocks.text: The tests send requests through FastAPI's `TestClient` and check the status codes, so any way of writing the rules that pydantic enforces passes. About ten lines.

cases.says: a valid request gets 200 and a negative budget gets 422
a budget of zero is a real budget, and a circuit cost below zero is refused
a circuit with zero miles is refused, while a short one is accepted
two circuits with the same id are refused
a request with no circuits is refused
a misspelled top-level field is refused instead of ignored
a misspelled field inside a circuit is refused instead of ignored
a circuit with an empty id is refused

origin.section: The Request Is a Pydantic Model, and FastAPI Refuses What It Does Not Fit

concepts: an endpoint is a method, a path and a Python function, and a TestClient calls it without a server
request rules live in the pydantic model, and FastAPI answers 422 to a body that breaks them
